prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment.

Findings and their definitions:
- Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion).
- Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent.
- Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis.
- Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count.
- Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space.
- Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count.

How to work:
1. Read the patient's image systematically first.
2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it.
3. Take the clinical indication into account.
4. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value.

Clinical indication: XXXX-year-old female, post XXXX closure

Similar cases (most similar first):

This may be artifact relating to calcification at the first rib costicartilage junction. There is minimal atelectasis in the right lung base. There is left-sided PICC line, the distal tip in the lower superior vena XXXX. The heart and pulmonary XXXX are normal. These contours are normal. IMPRESSION: 1. Vague nodular opacity near the anterior right first rib costicartilage junction. This may be calcification. 2. Minimal streaky atelectasis in the right lung base.
Case CXR3004 (similarity 0.923): FINDINGS: Frontal and lateral views of the chest show normal size and configuration of the cardiac silhouette. Left greater than right basilar opacity, probable atelectasis and/or scarring. No pleural effusion. IMPRESSION: Basilar atelectasis. Otherwise, no acute cardiac or pulmonary disease process.
Case CXR2585 (similarity 0.923): FINDINGS: Heart size and mediastinal contour are normal. Pulmonary vascularity is normal. There is mild blunting of the right costophrenic XXXX on the frontal view. There is also mild obscuration of the right cardiac XXXX. Airspace disease in expected location of right middle lobe also noted on the lateral view to No pleural effusion. Left lung clear. Degenerative changes spine. No pneumothorax. IMPRESSION: Right middle lobe airspace disease, which could represent pneumonia in the appropriate clinical setting.
Case CXR1502 (similarity 0.918): FINDINGS: The lungs are clear. There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax. The heart and mediastinum are normal. The skeletal structures are normal. IMPRESSION: No acute pulmonary disease.
Case CXR2096 (similarity 0.917): FINDINGS: Normal heart size and mediastinal contours. Clear lungs. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion. Unremarkable XXXX. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary process. .
Case CXR2320 (similarity 0.917): FINDINGS: The cardio mediastinal silhouette, pulmonary vascular pattern are within normal limits. No pneumothorax. No pneumonia. No pleural effusion. Mild degenerative changes mid thoracic spine. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease.
